web.runtimeCompatibility.title: OpenCodex Virtual Skeleton Diagnostics
web.runtimeCompatibility.pointsDescripti: Each modification point is organized by developer-facing feature group. Groups are for browsing only and do not affect enablement, fallback, or execution decisions.
web.runtimeCompatibility.empty: No modification points match the current filters.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.overallDes: Combines location, application, verification, activation, real hits, and fallback for one modification point. Groups are display-only and do not affect overall status.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.overall.he: The modification point is ready and its code path has executed at least once in this runtime.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.overall.re: Location, application, and verification completed, but the path has not executed in this runtime. This is not a failure.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.overall.pe: Location, application, verification, or activation is still incomplete, so no final result is available yet.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.overall.de: The point is using official behavior or another fallback. The feature can continue, but the enhancement may be unavailable.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.overall.un: Location, application, verification, or activation failed for the point.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.overall.di: The point is disabled by configuration or does not apply to this platform and runtime.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.adapterDes: Shows the complete Adapter chain used by the modification point, including its direct Adapter and dependent Adapters.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.locationDe: Location finds one unique target code path or capability that satisfies the current official runtime constraints. Application starts only after location succeeds.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.location.r: Candidate targets are being scanned and checked.
The expected number of targets was found and all constraints passed.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.location.u: Too few candidates were found, usually because this official runtime version does not contain the target.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.location.a: Multiple candidates were found, so the target cannot be selected safely.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.location.f: A candidate exists, but its structure, fingerprint, or another strict constraint failed.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.location.s: The target changed after location and the old result was rejected.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.applicatio: Application installs the compatibility implementation on the located target, such as wrapping a function, injecting a bridge, or rewriting cached content.
The point is registered, but application has not started.
The compatibility implementation is being installed.
The compatibility implementation was installed successfully.
A later application, verification, or activation step failed, so this change was undone in reverse order.
Installation threw an error or did not complete.
The point is disabled or does not apply to this environment, so application is skipped.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.verificati: Verification checks the resulting structure or capability after application so that executing a change is not mistaken for a change that actually works.
The post-application check has not completed.
The resulting structure or behavior passed its checks.
The point has no additional verification step; successful application is enough to become ready.
The post-application check failed, so the point is unavailable.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.activation: Activation means the Provider has started continuous capabilities such as an Observer, Listener, Hook layer, or protocol subscription. Successful activation means ready, not hit.
Continuous runtime capability has not started.
An Observer, Listener, Hook, or protocol subscription is starting.
Continuous runtime capability is active and waiting for a real business effect.
Continuous runtime capability failed to start, so the point is unavailable.
The capability was released after the page, runtime, or plugin lifecycle ended.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.exerciseDe: Hit status records whether the compatibility code path was used by real business behavior in this runtime and accumulates the call count. It distinguishes prepared code from code that actually worked.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.exercise.n: The implementation may be ready, but no business operation has reached this path in the current runtime. This is not a failure.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.exercise.a: The path executed. The page also shows the accumulated hit count.
web.runtimeCompatibility.help.exercise.d: The point is disabled or does not apply to this environment, so business hits are not counted.

web.runtimeCompatibility.group.workspace: Handles remote folder selection, workspace context, and worktree environments.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.remote-fi: Converts official local-file behavior into remote preview and download.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.smart-rou: Provides model catalog, routing, summary, and settings capabilities for smart scheduling.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.notificat: Notifications and hidden Runtime power savings
Adapts notifications and limits unnecessary background activity in the hidden Runtime.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.token-usa: Extracts and displays per-thread Token usage in the message interface.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.mobile-in: Handles the mobile sidebar, soft keyboard, iOS viewport, and touch behavior.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.renderer-: Adapts official UI structure, overlays, title bars, and Web containers.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.browser-p: Maps native desktop capabilities to browser-compatible capabilities.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.web-netwo: Handles compatibility for browser network requests and protocol data.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.project-n: Adjusts project, conversation, and navigation behavior.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.gateway-r: Manages the hidden official Runtime environment, Electron integration, and process lifecycle.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.gateway-i: Handles IPC routing and message shaping between Gateway and the official Runtime.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.official-: Applies verifiable optimizations to background work in the official main bundle.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.renderer-: Applies verifiable transformations to official Renderer HTML, CSP, and static chunks.
web.runtimeCompatibility.group.runner-pa: Generates, signs, and assembles background Runner artifacts for each platform.
web.runtimeCompatibility.adapter.adapter: Runtime view
Provides shared location, observation, measurement, and browser-view modification.
Protocol pipeline
Provides shared parsing, observation, transformation, and routing for runtime messages.
Runtime Hook
Provides shared wrapping for functions, properties, constructors, and module exports.
Static resource transformation
Provides shared location, transactional modification, and verification for static resources.
Runtime environment override
Provides shared management for environments, startup switches, and global capabilities.
Process behavior interception
Provides shared interception for child processes and system-open behavior.
Artifact build
Provides shared staging, assembly, signing, and commit for Runner artifacts.
Semantic view
Describes UI changes using stable views, slots, and virtual content.
Desktop Bridge
Maps official desktop interfaces to browser and Gateway capabilities.
Browser-native capabilities
Uses browser views and Hooks to emulate native desktop capabilities.
Network request adaptation
Intercepts network requests through shared Hooks and the protocol pipeline.
Mobile interaction adaptation
Unifies mobile events, viewport, and keyboard behavior on top of semantic views.
Official Runtime adaptation
Combines environment, Hook, and process capabilities to host the hidden official Runtime.
Official runtime environment
Declares pre-start environment and Chromium switches using official Runtime semantics.
Electron API
Declares runtime Hooks using Electron module and API semantics.
Project ordering
Declares Bridge Hooks using project and conversation ordering semantics.
Gateway IPC adaptation
Combines Hooks and the protocol pipeline to process official IPC.
App Server protocol adaptation
Implements App Server observation and transformation on the shared protocol pipeline.
Process bridge
Combines process interception and runtime Hooks to handle system behavior.
Semantic protocol
Normalizes raw protocol frames into stable domain messages.
Official main patch
Locates and transforms the official main bundle through static-resource transactions.
Official Renderer patch
Locates and transforms Renderer HTML and chunks through static-resource transactions.
Runner artifact
Assembles platform-specific Runners through artifact-build transactions.
